entries.test: Public investment analyses, GPU purchasing records and market reactions would establish Altman's contribution to Nvidia's rise relative to other major contributors besides Huang.
entries.note: “Nobody was more responsible” allows ties; “did more than anyone else” does not. The proposition also makes over-promising an explicit causal mechanism.
Calling the statement a bluff asserts private knowledge and intent; failed delivery alone would not establish that.
The present-tense component is explicitly probabilistic. The historical component also concerns Altman's private knowledge.

entries.test: Contemporaneous investor reports, valuations, GPU demand and reactions to scaling-related news would show whether expectations of AGI through scaling underpinned Nvidia's rise.
entries.note: This asserts a substantive market explanation, despite the evaluative wording.

entries.test: Nvidia's historical share prices and contemporaneous investment commentary would show whether its sharp rise tracked continuing confidence in scaling to AGI.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs give the temporal comparison a causal meaning.

entries.test: Altman's public launch statements and reproducible GPT-5 failures on tasks a qualified PhD can perform would settle the factual allegation.
entries.note: Marcus endorses the allegation of falsity, not the capability claim he attributes to Altman. “Wildly overhyped” is evaluative, but the capability allegation is testable.

entries.test: Timestamped launch-day user reports and reproducible examples would show whether users identified failures contradicting the attributed PhD-level capability claim by that night's end.
entries.note: “Within a day” relaxes “by the end of the night,” and plural “claims” broadens the specific claim at issue.

entries.test: Disclosed investments, financing agreements and reciprocal purchasing commitments would show whether circular arrangements accounted for an increasing share of AI industry financing.
entries.note: “Seemed” preserves an evidential qualification while identifying a concrete financial pattern.

entries.test: Public financial statements and linked investment and purchasing agreements would show whether AI market revenues depend on recycled financing rather than independent customer demand.
entries.note: “Warning sign” is evaluative, but the claim that circular financing props up the market has a factual reading.

entries.test: Contemporaneous analyst reports, investor surveys and fund flows would show whether confidence in AI investments declined, particularly after the September Oracle deal.
entries.note: The source reports that Marcus called the deal “peak bubble”; the proposition upgrades that label into an established market peak.

entries.test: Nvidia's share-price history from August 7, 2025 through February 4, 2026 would show whether its rapid rise had stalled without an outright crash.
entries.note: In context, “run out of gas” describes the observed plateau; it need not mean the stock can never rise again.
“Woke up” and “not magic” express disillusionment without specifying a testable capability or shared threshold.

entries.test: Public evaluations of contemporary LLMs across general intellectual tasks, including reproducible hallucinations and inconsistent answers, would establish their generality and reliability limits.
entries.note: The factual core concerns existing LLM capabilities and recurring failures; “great” supplies an evaluative concession.

entries.test: Public inference-cost estimates, competing model evaluations, switching behavior and pricing data would show operating expense and whether similar offerings make LLM services commercially interchangeable.
entries.note: The claim identifies competitive similarity as the mechanism of commoditization.

entries.test: Public LLM pricing histories and competitive analyses would show whether absent durable competitive barriers produce repeated competitive price cuts.
entries.note: The source presents a general causal relationship, with a forward implication for LLM makers.

entries.test: Public financial results of LLM businesses operating without AGI would show whether their profits remain modest or reach the immense levels anticipated by investors.
entries.note: This is a broad economic claim; imprecise profit thresholds do not by themselves make it uncheckable.
“My guess” explicitly qualifies the predicted declines.
The proposition broadens “these stocks” to AI tech stocks generally. Neither the hoped-for heights nor whose hopes count is specified.
“May” explicitly makes market readiness a possibility.
The opportunity for newcomers is qualified by “might actually be a chance.”
He expresses uncertainty about the worry, rather than firmly predicting that replacement will not occur.
